designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Odisha, governed by the Bengal, Agra and Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887 (as in force) read with the Orissa High Court of Judicature Order, 1948 and Orissa High Court Rules, 1948. Sessions courts try offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years. Odisha comprises 30 revenue districts and the subordinate judiciary is supervised by the Orissa High Court, Cuttack. Odia is the official language of the State subordinate courts under the Orissa Official Language Act, 1954.

party_designation.state: State of Odisha through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Odisha, Bhubaneswar

prayer_language.opening: It is, therefore, most humbly prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to:
prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the statements made in paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the statements made in paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Odia is the official language of the Odisha subordinate courts under the Orissa Official Language Act, 1954; pleadings before the High Court are in English. District court pleadings may be filed in English with Odia translation where required.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) before the Sessions Court must disclose any prior rejection by a Magistrate or co-ordinate court.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) must be accompanied by an affidavit, certified copy of the FIR and grounds of apprehension.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Orissa High Court Rules, 1948 to be filed at the first instance with requisite court-fee stamp.
All civil pleadings to be paginated, indexed and accompanied by a list of documents under Order VII / Order VIII CPC.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as in force in Odisha with State amendments; ad valorem fee structure applies to civil suits.
Atrocities (SC/ST), POCSO and NDPS cases are tried by designated Special Courts notified by the State Government — typically the District & Sessions Judge at the district headquarters.
Designated Special Courts also exist for offences under the Odisha Protection of Interests of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act, 2011.
Cuttack hosts the principal seat of the Orissa High Court; the District & Sessions Court at Cuttack and Khurda (Bhubaneswar) handle the largest dockets.
e_filing_note: e-Filing is operational at Cuttack, Khurda and Bhubaneswar district courts via the eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
